text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- A ministry of trade committee is planning a restructure of the state-owned financing companies; Finnish Export Credit may come up for sale and Kera and other specialist financing companies may be bundled together.
- Finnish managers put little weight on moral issues and consider a strong market economy to be a cure for unemployment, a study by Centre for Finnish Business and Policy Studies (EVA) shows.
- Swedish state-owned power producer Vattenfall did not gain a majority of Finnish regional utility Savon Voima.
- State subsidies to household work were approved in parliament on Monday; the experiment will start in November.
- Finnish political parties disagree over electoral districts in European elections.
- Finnair's decision to buy Airbus aircraft was fully justified, official says, responding to criticism that it was unlogical since Finnair recently ordered Boeing planes for its holiday traffic.

- Danish Unibank targets a 10 percent share of the Finnish market, CEO Thorleif Krarup says on a visit to Finland, adding he expects only six or seven banks to rule in Nordic banking in a couple of years.
- Finnish forestry companies plan to raise fine paper prices by five to 12 percent next autumn.
- Swedish construction group Skanska has lost money and time as activists have occupied and stopped tearing down two wooden houses where Skanska is a bloc of flats, Skanska official says.
- The Finnish clothing industry is regaining balance but many companies are still forced to move manufacturing to countries with cheaper labour, sector representatives say.
- First women army pilots to be airborne in August.

- The environmental ministry's Natura 2000-programme of environmental protection must not hinder traffic development, ministry of traffic says, calling for some of the planned protection areas to be excluded from the programme.
